newsitem.title: UK: British govt plans to privatise London Underground.
newsitem.headline: British govt plans to privatise London Underground.

text.p: Britain's Conservative government said on Tuesday it wanted to privatise London's Underground rail system -- the oldest such network in the world and the transport lifeline of the capital.

Transport Secretary George Young told BBC radio he would be making a statement in parliament later in the day but said he believed that the future of London Underground rested "in the private sector."
The proposals to sell off London Underground, popularly known as the Tube, will form a key part of the Conservative Party's campaign strategy for national elections which must be held by May 22.
It follows the privatisation of formerly state-run industries such as steel, railways, water, gas, electricity, telephone and coal.
The underground network, some of which dates back to 1865, comprises 248 stations on 11 lines that criss-cross one of Europe's biggest cities and transport 2.7 million people a day.

Young said privatisation would allow more money to be invested in the network and allow London Underground to plan for the long-term and not compete for public funds with other government departments.
He said details of the sale had yet to be finalised.
Last week, London Underground chiefs complained of massive under-investment from the government and listed hundreds of repair and improvement projects that have been shelved as a result.

They told politicians that funding for the next three years is about 700 million pounds ($1.1 billion) less than they had expected. But Young denied any reductions had been made in next year's budget.

"I think what we have in mind will be very popular with voters, very popular with passengers because it will improve the quality of public transport here in London," Young said. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
